# SPI Host Core FSM Behavioral Specification

## 1. Overview

This module is the core controller for the SPI host. It accepts SPI command-segment descriptors, controls the SPI bus signals (serial clock and chip selects), and coordinates data movement through the SPI data path.

The module must:

- Generate the SPI serial clock at the configured rate and polarity.
- Assert and deassert chip selects with the required timing.
- Support Standard, Dual, and Quad SPI data-width modes.
- Support transmit-only, receive-only, dummy-cycle, and bidirectional segments.
- Support back-to-back segments with chip select held active.
- Stall safely when the transmit or receive data path is not ready.
- Provide status and flow-control outputs to the rest of the SPI host.

The SPI host supports single data rate operation only; it does not perform double data rate transfers.

---

## 2. Reset and Enable

### 2.1 Hardware Reset

On hardware reset, the module must:

- Become inactive and idle.
- Deassert all chip selects.
- Drive the serial clock to its idle low level.
- Disable all SPI data output drivers.
- Clear all transaction progress counters.
- Be ready to accept a command once the block is enabled.

### 2.2 Software Reset

A software reset request must:

- Abandon any transaction in progress.
- Return the module to the inactive idle state.
- Deassert all chip selects.
- Disable all SPI data output drivers.
- Cause the module to become ready again after the reset request is released.

The configured clock polarity may remain; therefore, after software reset the serial clock may return to the configured idle level, which may be high if the current polarity setting requires it.

### 2.3 Block Enable

The module must not accept commands or generate SPI activity while the block-enable input is deasserted.

If block enable is deasserted during an active transaction:

- The module must suspend in its current state.
- It must not accept new commands.
- It must not advance the transaction.
- The chip select and serial clock outputs must hold their current values.

When block enable is reasserted, the transaction must resume from the suspended point.

---

## 3. Command Interface and Acceptance

### 3.1 Command Segment Descriptor

The module accepts one command-segment descriptor at a time. Each descriptor must provide:

- The target chip-select identifier.
- Configuration settings for the target device:
  - Clock polarity.
  - Clock phase.
  - Full-cycle sampling mode.
  - Clock divider.
  - Chip-select lead timing.
  - Chip-select trail timing.
  - Chip-select idle timing.
- Segment length.
- Segment direction:
  - Dummy.
  - Receive-only.
  - Transmit-only.
  - Bidirectional.
- Segment speed:
  - Standard.
  - Dual.
  - Quad.
- A flag indicating whether the chip select must remain active after the segment completes.

### 3.2 Command Acceptance

The module must accept a command only when:

- It asserts command-ready.
- The command-valid input is asserted.
- No stall condition is active.

All descriptor and configuration fields are captured when the command is accepted.

The module must assert command-ready only when it is safe to accept a new segment:

- In the inactive idle state.
- When waiting in the chip-select-active idle state and the incoming command targets the same chip select.
- At the end of the inter-transaction idle delay.
- When the previous transaction has been closed and the next command is already waiting.

Command-ready must be suppressed while a stall is active.

### 3.3 Pending Commands and State Bypass

If a command is already waiting when the module reaches the end of an idle period, the module may proceed directly into the next operational phase without first entering an idle state.

Similarly, if a continuation command is already waiting at the end of a chip-select-active segment, the module may continue directly into the next segment without entering the chip-select-active idle state.

---

## 4. Chip-Select and Transaction Framing

### 4.1 Chip-Select Behavior

Chip selects are active-low.

For each transaction, the module must:

- Assert only the chip select corresponding to the target device.
- Keep all other chip selects deasserted.
- Keep the selected chip select low for the entire transaction, including lead and trail periods.

### 4.2 Lead Timing

After a chip select is asserted, the module must hold the serial clock idle for at least the configured lead time before producing the first serial clock edge.

This lead time must not be shorter than the configured lead value expressed in half-serial-clock periods.

### 4.3 Trail Timing

After the final serial clock edge of a transaction, the module must hold the chip select low for at least the configured trail time before deasserting it.

This trail time must not be shorter than the configured trail value expressed in half-serial-clock periods.

### 4.4 Inter-Transaction Idle Timing

After the chip select is deasserted, all chip selects must remain high for at least the configured idle time before the next chip select may be asserted.

This idle time must not be shorter than the configured idle value expressed in half-serial-clock periods.

### 4.5 Configuration Changes

If the configuration supplied with the next command differs from the configuration currently in use, the module must not simply proceed with the next segment.

The module must:

- Finish any timing requirements of the previous configuration.
- Hold all chip selects high.
- Apply the new configuration only while no chip select is active.
- Insert an additional configuration-switch idle delay before starting the next transaction.
- Ensure no serial clock pulses are generated during the configuration switch.

The configuration-switch delay must satisfy the idle-time requirement of the new configuration.

### 4.6 Back-to-Back Segments with Chip Select Held Active

If the previous segment enables “chip select active after segment” and the next segment targets the same chip select, the module must:

- Keep the chip select asserted.
- Skip the lead, trail, and idle delays normally inserted between transactions.
- Continue generating serial clocks for the next segment without a gap.

If no next segment is available when the current segment ends, the module must:

- Keep the chip select asserted.
- Place the serial clock in the idle level.
- Wait in the chip-select-active idle state.
- Assert command-ready so firmware may submit the next segment.

This allows complex multi-segment commands to be assembled without deasserting the chip select.

### 4.7 Switching Targets While Chip Select Is Held Active

If a command is presented while the module is in the chip-select-active idle state and the command targets a different chip select, the module must not acknowledge it immediately.

The module must first:

- Terminate the current transaction.
- Apply the normal trail delay while the old chip select is still low.
- Deassert the old chip select.
- Hold all chip selects high for the required idle time.
- Possibly apply the configuration-switch delay if the new target configuration also changes.

Only after this closing sequence may the module accept the new command and assert the new chip select.

---

## 5. Serial Clock Generation

### 5.1 Clock Rate

The serial clock frequency must be derived from the input clock and the configured clock divider.

With a divider value of zero, the serial clock period must be two input-clock periods.

The serial clock must toggle only during the active clock portion of a segment. It must not toggle during lead, trail, idle, configuration-switch, or stall periods.

### 5.2 Clock Polarity and Phase

The module must support all combinations of clock polarity and clock phase:

- Clock polarity selects the idle level of the serial clock:
  - Polarity 0: idle low, active pulses are positive.
  - Polarity 1: idle high, active pulses are negative.
- Clock phase selects the data timing relationship:
  - Phase 0: the first output bit is presented when the chip select is asserted, and sampling occurs on the leading edge.
  - Phase 1: the first output bit is presented on the first serial clock edge, and sampling occurs on the trailing edge.

The module must align its data-path control pulses so that the shift register behavior conforms to the selected phase.

### 5.3 Full-Cycle Sampling

In normal operation, incoming data is sampled one half serial-clock period after the edge that causes the remote device to drive the data.

In full-cycle mode, the module must delay the sampling event by an additional half serial-clock period. The resulting sample point is one full serial clock period after the data-driving edge.

Full-cycle mode affects only sampling; it must not change the serial clock or chip-select timing.

---

## 6. Segment Execution

### 6.1 Segment Length

The length field defines the number of bytes to transfer for:

- Transmit-only segments.
- Receive-only segments.
- Bidirectional segments.

For dummy-only segments, the length field defines the number of serial clock cycles for which the bus is held in the dummy state and no data is transferred.

### 6.2 Segment Direction

The module must support the following segment directions:

- **Dummy**: Generate the requested number of serial clock cycles. Do not request transmit data, do not capture received data, and keep all data output drivers disabled.
- **Transmit-only**: Load transmit bytes and shift them out. Do not generate receive transfers.
- **Receive-only**: Generate clocks, sample incoming data, and produce receive byte transfers. Do not request transmit data and keep data output drivers disabled.
- **Bidirectional**: Simultaneously transmit and receive one byte per byte time. This is allowed only in Standard speed.

The module must never perform a bidirectional transfer in Dual or Quad speed.

### 6.3 Segment Speed

The module must support three data widths:

- **Standard**: one data line used, one bit shifted per serial clock edge.
- **Dual**: two data lines used, two bits shifted per serial clock edge.
- **Quad**: four data lines used, four bits shifted per serial clock edge.

The module must communicate the current speed to the data path so that the shift register can select the correct lane count and shift amount.

### 6.4 Transmit Byte Transfers

For transmit-only and bidirectional segments, the module must issue a transmit-byte request at the beginning of each byte time.

The module must not issue such requests when:

- The segment is receive-only.
- The segment is dummy.
- A stall is active.

The transmit-byte request must be accompanied by a last-write indication when the byte is the final byte of the segment.

The last-write indication must be valid for the byte being requested, and must be accurate for both clock-phase settings.

### 6.5 Receive Byte Transfers

For receive-only and bidirectional segments, the module must issue a receive-byte transfer when a byte has been fully received.

The module must not issue receive transfers when:

- The segment is transmit-only.
- The segment is dummy.
- A stall is active.

The receive-byte transfer must be accompanied by a last-read indication when the byte is the final byte of the segment.

The last-read indication must be accurate for both clock-phase settings.

### 6.6 Shift Events

The module must issue a shift event for each data beat within a byte.

- In Standard speed, one shift event is needed per serial clock edge.
- In Dual speed, one shift event advances two data bits.
- In Quad speed, one shift event advances four data bits.

Shift events must be suppressed during stalls.

### 6.7 Sample Events

The module must issue sample events so that incoming data is captured at the correct point in the serial clock period.

Sampling must be suppressed during stalls.

If full-cycle mode is enabled, the sample event timing must be delayed by one half serial-clock period relative to normal sampling.

---

## 7. Data Output Enable Control

### 7.1 Output Drivers While Chip Select Is Inactive

When all chip selects are high, all SPI data output drivers must be disabled.

### 7.2 Output Drivers During Active Segments

When a chip select is active, data output drivers must be enabled according to the segment speed and direction:

- **Standard**: The first data line may be driven; all other data lines remain disabled.
- **Dual**: The first two data lines may be driven; the remaining data lines remain disabled.
- **Quad**: All four data lines may be driven.
- **Receive-only and dummy segments**: No data output drivers may be enabled.

### 7.3 End-of-Segment Output Enable Behavior

When a Standard-speed transmit-capable segment ends and the following segment is receive-only or dummy, the module must not disable the data output drivers early.

For this transition, the transmit output enables must remain asserted through the final bit period of the last transmitted byte, even if the next segment descriptor disables transmit mode.

---

## 8. Flow Control and Stall Behavior

### 8.1 Transmit Stall

If the module needs to request a transmit byte but the transmit data path is not ready to supply one, it must:

- Assert the transmit-stall status.
- Freeze all state.
- Stop serial clock toggling.
- Hold chip selects in their current states.
- Suppress all data-path control pulses.
- Suppress command-ready.

Transmit-stall must remain asserted until the transmit data path becomes ready.

### 8.2 Receive Stall

If the module needs to produce a receive byte but the receive data path is not ready to accept one, it must:

- Assert the receive-stall status.
- Freeze all state.
- Stop serial clock toggling.
- Hold chip selects in their current states.
- Suppress all data-path control pulses.
- Suppress command-ready.

Receive-stall must remain asserted until the receive data path becomes ready.

### 8.3 Effect of Stall

While any stall condition is active:

- No transaction progress is allowed.
- No byte transfers may be issued.
- No shift or sample events may be issued.
- No commands may be accepted.
- The serial clock and chip-select outputs must hold their current values.

When the stall condition clears, the transaction must resume from the exact point at which it was suspended.

---

## 9. Status Outputs

The module must provide the following status behavior:

- **Active status**:
  - Low when the module is waiting for a command, whether in the inactive idle state or in the chip-select-active idle state.
  - High while any transaction framing is in progress, including lead, clock, trail, idle-delay, and configuration-switch phases.

- **Command-ready status**:
  - Indicates that the module can accept a new command-segment descriptor.
  - Must be suppressed during stalls.

- **Current speed output**:
  - Must reflect the speed of the current segment so the data path can select Standard, Dual, or Quad operation.

- **Current full-cycle output**:
  - Must reflect whether the current configuration requires full-cycle sampling.

- **Stall status outputs**:
  - Must indicate whether the module is stalled waiting on the transmit data path or the receive data path.
